# Draft markers {#sec-g-draft}

A draft book carries the questions each section must answer, and marks the sections still to be written. Neither shows in a normal render.

## Draft questions {#sec-g-draft-questions}

Write the questions a section must answer as an HTML comment directly after it. The comment starts with `<!-- Q` on its own line. Each question is a line that starts with `- `. The comment ends with `-->`.

````markdown
<!-- Q
- What fraction of samples passed quality control?
- Which threshold removed the most samples?
-->
````

This section carries a real block of draft questions below this paragraph. In a normal render it is invisible.

<!-- Q
- Can a reader write a question block from this description alone?
- Is the closing marker described exactly?
-->

## How the questions render {#sec-g-draft-render}

| Render | Command | What the reader sees |
|---|---|---|
| Normal | `quarto render --profile gallery` | Nothing. The comment stays a comment. |
| Draft | `quarto render --profile gallery,draft` | A collapsed tip, titled as draft questions, with a numbered list. |

: How draft questions render in each profile. {#tbl-g-draft-render}

The filter `filters/draft-questions.lua` does the swap. It runs only when the metadata flag `draft-questions` is true, which the draft profile sets.

<!-- Q
- Does the draft render show this block as a collapsed callout?
-->

## Sections still to be written {#sec-g-draft-tbw}

::: {.callout-important}
## To be written
Robustness to the choice of normalisation. Compare depth scaling with an alternative, on the same thresholds.
:::

````markdown
::: {.callout-important}
## To be written
Robustness to the choice of normalisation. Compare depth scaling with an alternative, on the same thresholds.
:::
````

Use it for a section the author must still fill. Unlike a question block, it shows in every render, because a reader must know the section is missing.

## Opting out of a register flag {#sec-g-draft-optout}

The register guard flags interpretive constructions outside the synthesis chapter. Sometimes a flagged sentence is correct where it stands, for example a quotation from a study protocol. Put an opt-out comment on the line before it:

````markdown
<!-- register-ok: quoting the hypothesis from the study protocol -->
The protocol states the hypothesis in its own words.
````

The reason is mandatory. An opt-out comment with an empty reason is itself reported as a violation. The reason tells a reviewer why the rule does not apply here.

<!-- Q
- Is it clear that an opt-out without a reason fails the check?
-->
